description: How far along a Robinhood Chain token is, read from the chain: whether its contract is deployed, when its first tokens were minted, and when the first pools for it were created on Uniswap. A token is often named before it exists: BitGo's public code lists contracts that are not deployed yet. Each step that follows leaves a dated record on chain, and this tool reads them. Pass the token's contract address as `token`; the `contract` of an entry from brainchain_custody_additions works. `token` can also be a symbol or name, such as RLUSD or Ripple USD, looked up on BitGo's lists for Robinhood Chain; when none there goes by it, on the lists the BrainChain MCP dataset records (Trust Wallet, MetaMask, LI.FI, CoinGecko, KuCoin and Gate); and when none there does either, among every token with a Uniswap pool by the symbol its contract gives itself (`pool index`). When exactly one token goes by it, `lookup` in the answer names the `contract` it stands for and its `source`, and for one found in the dataset the `dataset` day, block and manifest read; when several do, the answer lists them as `candidates`, each with its `source`, and reads nothing more. A symbol is whatever the token's deployer chose, so check the contract before relying on one found in the pool index. `deployed` says whether a contract is at the address. For a deployed token, `token` holds the `name` and `symbol` the contract gives itself, its `decimals` and its `totalSupply`, counted in tokens and not in the token's smallest unit. Whoever deployed the contract chose the name and symbol, so they do not prove which token it is. `firstMint` is the first time tokens were created: `at`, the `block`, the `transaction` and `to`, the address that received them. It is left out for a token with nothing minted. `pools` lists the first pool created for the token on Uniswap v4 and on Uniswap v3, earliest first: the `venue`, `at`, the `block`, the `transaction` and `pairedWith`, the other token's contract address, or ETH. Only the first pool on each venue is listed. Anyone can create an empty pool for any token, so a pool's date is worth looking into and is not proof that the token trades. Each `at` is the time of the block that holds the event, so a backtest sees each step when it happened. `readAt` is when the chain was read. The tool answers one request at a time. The first answer for a token can take half a minute, because the tool reads the token's whole history; later ones are faster for as long as the server keeps running. An answer that is not ready after 45 seconds says so, and asking again goes on from where it stopped. Free, no key and no payment. Not advice.

token.description: The token's contract address on Robinhood Chain, 0x followed by 40 hex characters, or its symbol or name, such as RLUSD.

title: How far along a Robinhood Chain token is
